authority.abi: No C ABI change. No exported symbol, extern "C" signature or #[repr(C)] layout changed.
external_contracts: bio_lib.c:83 OPENSSL_zalloc(sizeof(*bio)) -- the BIO block must come from the CRYPTO allocator seam so CRYPTO_set_mem_functions observes it.
bio_lib.c:99,110 new_ex_data failure frees the block only; create failure frees ex_data and the block and must NOT run the method destroy.
bio_lib.c:126-147 the last reference is consumed before BIO_CB_FREE; a veto leaves the object leaked, not restored.
bio_lib.c:845-859 BIO_free_all reads refcount and next_bio before releasing, and stops after an element whose pre-free count exceeds one.
bss_mem.c:95-165 memory BIO: buf and readp are separate blocks, b->ptr is published only after both are established, shutdown==0/init==0 deliberately leak buf (authority parity).

boundaries.before: Allocated with Box::new and released with Box::from_raw. The block bypassed CRYPTO_set_mem_functions entirely: an installed allocator hook never saw the allocation, a refused allocation was not observable, and the seam accounting was silently wrong.
boundaries.after: CRYPTO_zalloc(size_of::<Bio>()) with ptr::write initialisation, released by CRYPTO_free at the authority's site. No reference is formed before initialisation.
boundaries.mechanism: ELIMINATED: a BIO block that the allocator seam cannot see is no longer constructible.

boundaries.before: A &mut Bio was live across BIO_CB_FREE and the method destroy. Both are C function pointers a caller can set; a re-entrant BIO_free through the same pointer would have had two exclusive borrows of one object.
boundaries.after: The last-reference sentinel is claimed first; every field is re-read through the raw pointer; no &mut outlives either callback.
boundaries.mechanism: ELIMINATED: two exclusive borrows of one Bio across a callback are no longer expressible.
boundaries.state: FIXED (author) + INDEPENDENTLY_CHECKED (reviewer, Miri SB and TB)

boundaries.operation: safety documentation of the chain walk
boundaries.before: The # Safety claimed a dangling non-NULL link was handled; it is caller UB because the walk reads the link before it can test it. The doc also did not state that a free callback must not release the remaining chain.
boundaries.after: The contract states every non-NULL link must be live and that a free callback/destroy must not release or unlink the tail.
boundaries.mechanism: RELOCATED to an explicit ABI contract (an arbitrary-chain precondition is not representable in safe Rust).
